=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2023 Question 1 (9 points total).
Topic: Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results with Experimental Design (PHO Signaling Pathway).
Pathological/Biological Context: In eukaryotic microorganisms, high extracellular inorganic phosphate (Pi) causes Pho4 to be phosphorylated by the Pho80-Pho85 complex, suppressing Pho target genes (like PHO1). Low Pi inhibits Pho80-Pho85 via Pho81, allowing Pho4 to induce target gene expression.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) Describe that adding a charged phosphate group alters the tertiary folding/shape of the protein; (1 pt) Explain signal amplification as each enzyme acting on multiple protein copies.
- Part (b): (1 pt) Identify dependent variable (APase activity or PHO1 mRNA level); (1 pt) Justify wild-type control to ensure differences stem only from introduced mutations; (1 pt) Justify single mutations to test each component's effect separately.
- Part (c): (1 pt) Identify Wild-type in low-Pi as highest PHO1 mRNA; (1 pt) Calculate percent change in APase activity [(17.3 - 0.5)/0.5 * 100 = 3,360% or (0.5 - 17.3)/17.3 * 100 = -97%].
- Part (d): (1 pt) Predict PHO1 will be expressed with nonfunctional Pho85 in high-Pi; (1 pt) Reason that nonfunctional Pho85 cannot phosphorylate/inhibit Pho4.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1A) ===
a. The addition of a charged phosphate group likely changes the tertiary folding structure of a protein, and since structure determines function, a change in its folding due to the phosphate group could cause the protein to become inactive. A signal is amplified when there is a chain reaction, likely a phosphorylation cascade. One reaction leads to another, often increasing the size and impacts of the reactions as they continue or pass along.
b. One dependent variable is the activity of APase. In using a wild-type strain to create the mutant strain, the researchers can be sure that the only mutation is the one they induced and all other genes are consistent with the wild type. Further, by using mutant strains that had only a single component mutated, they could know that any significant differences in enzyme activity were for sure caused by that one mutation since everything else was the same.
c. The wild-type yeast in the Low-Pi environment had the highest relative amount of PHO1 mRNA. Percent change: (17.3 - 0.5) / 0.5 * 100 = 3360%.
d. A mutation resulting in nonfunctional Pho85 would allow transcription of the Pho target gene despite a High Pi environment. This is because Pho85 would not be able to form the Pho80-Pho85 complex and phosphorylyze Pho4. Therefore, Pho4 will transcribe the Pho target genes even when it should not, leading to increased PHO1 expression.
feedback:
Total Score: 8/9 points.
- Part (a) [1/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for correctly describing that the addition of a phosphate group alters the tertiary folding structure of a protein. Did NOT earn the 2nd point because the explanation of signal amplification described a generic chain reaction cascade without explicitly stating that each enzyme can act on multiple copies of a target protein.
- Part (b) [3/3 pts]: Earned all 3 pts. Correctly identified 'APase activity' as a dependent variable, accurately justified the use of wild-type background to eliminate genetic background variations, and clearly explained that mutating single components isolates the causative effect of each mutation.
- Part (c) [2/2 pts]: Earned 2 pts. Accurately identified 'wild-type yeast in low-Pi environment' as producing highest PHO1 mRNA, and correctly calculated the percent change as 3,360%.
- Part (d) [2/2 pts]: Earned 2 pts. Correctly predicted that PHO1 target genes will be expressed/transcribed and justified that nonfunctional Pho85 cannot phosphorylate Pho4 to inhibit it.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2023 Question 1 (PHO Signaling Pathway).
Rubric Requirements: Describe structure change (1 pt); Explain enzyme amplification (1 pt); Identify dependent variable (1 pt); Justify wild-type control (1 pt); Justify single mutation (1 pt); Identify wild-type low-Pi (1 pt); Calculate percent change (+3360% or -97%) (1 pt); Predict target gene expression (1 pt); Justify Pho4 non-inhibition (1 pt).

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1B) ===
a) A charged phosphate group can inhibit the proteins receptor. A signal can be amplified during signal transduction pathway through the electron transport chain.
b) A dependent variable is the APase Activity of the strains of yeast. It was important for the researchers to use the wild-type strain to create the mutant strain to ensure no other mutations were present in the strain. It was important for the researchers to only mutate a single component of the pathway so that they can accurately determine whether or not it is causing differences in APase activity/amount of PHO1 mRNA. If multiple components were mutated, the researchers would not know which component is causing the difference.
c) wild-type, low-pi environment. |0.5 - 17.3| / 17.3 * 100 = 97.11%.
d) This would decrease PHO1 expression blc it will stop the conversion of ATP to ADP, which is necessary for PHO1 formation.
feedback:
Total Score: 5/9 points.
- Part (a) [0/2 pts]: Failed both points. Incorrectly described phosphate action as 'inhibiting protein receptors' without mentioning structural/folding alteration. Incorrectly defined signal amplification as occurring through the 'electron transport chain'.
- Part (b) [3/3 pts]: Earned all 3 pts for correctly identifying APase activity as the dependent variable, justifying wild-type use to ensure no background mutations exist, and explaining that single mutations allow pinpointing which specific component causes observed differences.
- Part (c) [2/2 pts]: Earned 2 pts. Correctly identified the wild-type low-Pi environment and accurately calculated percent change as 97.11% (accepted rounded equivalent of -97%).
- Part (d) [0/2 pts]: Failed both points. Incorrectly predicted that PHO1 expression would decrease, and falsely reasoned that it stops ATP-to-ADP conversion required for PHO1 formation.

The researchers mutated only one component in each strain to see a difference when certain independent variables are added.
c) The highest relative amount of PHO1 mRNA resulted from the wild type yeast strain in a low-Pi environment. The percent change in APase activity in wildtype yeast cells in a high-Pi environment compared to a low-Pi environment is 34.6%.

feedback:

Missed both justification points because the claims ('to have a control group to compare data to' and 'see a difference when independent variables are added') were far too generic and lacked experimental specificity.
- Part (c) [1/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for identifying wild-type yeast in low-Pi. Missed the calculation point due to an incorrect math result of 34.6%.
- Part (d) [0/2 pts]: Failed both points. Incorrectly predicted a decrease in PHO1 levels and provided flawed reasoning regarding lack of signal amplification.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2023 Question 2 (9 points total).
Topic: Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results with Graphing (CO2 Levels, Mitochondria Density & Non-Mendelian Genetics).
Experimental Setup: 6 plant species evaluated for mitochondria density under normal vs. elevated CO2. Cross performed between pollen from white-striped leaf plant (mitochondrial DNA mutation) and ovules from green leaf plant.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) Describe inner mitochondrial membrane role (ETC location / ATP synthase / proton gradient establishment).
- Part (b): (4 pts total) Bar graph construction (1 pt); Correct axis labels with units [Mitochondria per 100 um2 / Species] (1 pt); Accurately plotted data points and +/-2SEx error bars (1 pt); Determine that 'All species' show a significant difference (1 pt).
- Part (c): (1 pt) Describe positive correlation between CO2 level and mitochondria density.
- Part (d): (1 pt) Predict offspring leaves will be green; (1 pt) Reason that mitochondria/organelle DNA are maternally inherited via ovules; (1 pt) Explain that CO2 environment changes affect gene expression regulating organelle numbers.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 2A) ===
a) The inner mitochondrial membrane (cristae) is used for the electron transport chain, which is essential to create the proton concentration gradient for the production of ATP.
b) [Bar graph plotted with clear labels, key, and accurate error bars]. All the species show significant difference in the number of mitochondria between normal and elevated levels of CO2.
c) Levels of CO2 and average number of mitochondria per unit area of a cell have positive correlation because the plants with higher CO2 levels have greater number of mitochondria per unit.
d) Phenotype of the leaves of the offspring would be green. That is because mutations in mitochondrial DNA can only be passed from the female parent. Plants with same genotype are able to differ in structure and/or number of organelles in response to levels of CO2 because different factors play a role in phenotypes and gene expression of organisms. Since CO2 is an important factor, it could have an effect.
feedback:
Total Score: 9/9 points (Perfect Score).
- Part (a) [1/1 pt]: Correctly described inner membrane role as the site for the electron transport chain and proton gradient establishment.
- Part (b) [4/4 pts]: Earned all 4 points. Constructed a clean bar graph, included full axis labels with correct measurement units and legend, accurately plotted data points with 2SEx error bars, and correctly concluded that 'all species' show a significant difference.
- Part (c) [1/1 pt]: Accurately described the relationship as a positive correlation.
- Part (d) [3/3 pts]: Earned all 3 points. Correctly predicted green leaves, justified maternal inheritance of mitochondrial DNA from the female parent (ovule), and clearly explained that CO2 levels influence gene expression to alter organelle counts.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2023 Question 2 (CO2 Levels & Mitochondria).
Rubric Requirements: Describe inner membrane role (1 pt); Bar graph format (1 pt); Axis labeling with units (1 pt); Accurate data/error bars (1 pt); Determine 'All species' differ (1 pt); Describe positive correlation (1 pt); Predict green leaves (1 pt); Justify maternal inheritance (1 pt); Explain environmental gene expression (1 pt).

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 2B) ===
a) The role of the inner mitochondrial membrane is to allow molecules to move in and out during cellular respiration. In cellular respiration, the selectively permeable membrane lets in CO2 and other substances, while releasing O2.
b) [Bar graph drawn with labels and key]. All of the species show a difference in number of mitochondria between normal and elevated as the error bars don't overlap, illustrating significant difference.
c) Based on Table 1, as level of CO2 increases, the average number of mitochondria per unit area increases as more are used to do cellular respiration.
d) The possible phenotypes would be a plant with green leaves or a plant with white-striped leaves. Using the Punnet square, we can see that there is 50% it can be striped and 50% it can be green. Plants with same genotype can differ in response to CO2 levels because if there are more CO2, to absorb more, the plant would need to change its structure, so they have more stomata openings to get CO2... Once they have more CO2, they would need more organelles such as chloroplasts and mitochondria...
feedback:
Total Score: 5/9 points.
- Part (a) [0/1 pt]: Failed. Incorrectly described inner membrane function as letting CO2 in and releasing O2 (swapping cellular gas exchange functions).
- Part (b) [4/4 pts]: Earned all 4 points. Graph had appropriate bar format, full labels, accurate error bars, and correctly concluded all species showed differences.
- Part (c) [1/1 pt]: Earned 1 pt for describing that higher CO2 levels result in an increased average number of mitochondria.
- Part (d) [0/3 pts]: Failed all 3 points in (d). Falsely predicted a 50/50 Mendelian split using a Punnett square, failed to identify maternal organelle inheritance, and gave a vague stomata explanation rather than referencing environmental influence on gene expression.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2024 Question 1 (9 points total).
Topic: Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results with Experimental Design (Meiotic Crossing Over, Hotspots & Kinetochore Proteins).
Experimental Context: Homologous yeast chromosome 8 pair engineered with RFP and GFP markers. Kinetochore proteins CTF and IML tested at hotspots. Follow-up experiment used DNA-binding mutant CTF.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (i) (1 pt) Describe S phase as replicating/duplicating DNA; (ii) (1 pt) Explain single fluorescent marker in haploid cells as receiving a sister chromatid that did not undergo crossing over.
- Part (b): (i) (1 pt) Identify Group 1 / 'None' as control; (ii) (1 pt) Justify modified CTF control to determine if DNA binding itself inhibits crossing over versus mere protein presence; (iii) (1 pt) Identify independent variable (type of CTF used / presence or absence of CTF).
- Part (c): (1 pt) Describe CTF attachment as decreasing crossing over frequency compared to IML attachment.
- Part (d): (i) (1 pt) Predict 0 or 2 copies / 1 extra or 1 less copy of chromosome 8 in daughter cells; (ii) (1 pt) Reason that reduced crossing over increases nondisjunction probability; (iii) (1 pt) Explain that hotspots increase genetic diversity, improving population adaptation under selection.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1A) ===
(a)(i) The S phase of interphase is where the DNA is replicated in preparation for cell division...
(a)(ii) Some haploid cells formed after meiosis will only have one fluorescent marker and not both because not all chromatids experience crossing over. In the two homologous Chromosome 8's, only the two close together chromatids experienced crossing over, where the other 2 didnt...
(b)(i) Group 1 - with no kinetochore proteins attached to the hot spot - is the control group for the scientist's first experiment.
(b)(ii) The scientists used a modified CTF protein that is unable to bind to DNA as a control because it can show them that it is the CTF protein binding to the DNA that is causing the decrease in frequency of crossing over and not another variable.
(b)(iii) The independent variable in the follow up experiment is the presence or absence of the either modified or unmodified CTF protein.
(c) There is a decrease in the frequency of crossing over when CTF is attached to the chromosome 8 hot spot compared to the frequency relatively not changing... when IML is attached...
(d)(i) When CTF is attached to the hotspot, the number of copies of Chromosome 8 is likely to be different and not the usual one chromosome 8 per haploid daughter cell.
(d)(ii) This is because crossing over is required in meiosis I for homologous chromosomes to properly align. Since CTF protein decreases the frequency of crossing over, there is then a higher chance that the chromosomes dont align properly, leading to potential nondisjunction events...
(d)(iii) The presence of hotspots could increase the likelihood that a population will survive in the presence of selective pressures because crossing over leads to genetic variation... resulting in each haploid gamete carrying a completely new and different genome...
feedback:
Total Score: 8/9 points.
- Part (a) [2/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for describing S phase DNA replication and 1 pt for explaining that non-recombined chromatids yield single-marker gametes.
- Part (b) [3/3 pts]: Earned all 3 pts. Identified Group 1 as control, correctly justified that the DNA-binding mutant CTF verifies if DNA binding causes crossing over reduction, and accurately identified the independent variable.
- Part (c) [1/1 pt]: Correctly described that CTF attachment decreases crossing over frequency relative to IML.
- Part (d) [2/3 pts]: Missed (d)(i) point because response stated copy numbers would be 'different and not the usual one' without predicting explicit numeric outcomes (0 or 2 copies / 1 extra or 1 missing). Earned (d)(ii) for linking reduced crossing over to improper alignment and nondisjunction. Earned (d)(iii) for explaining genetic variation and selective fitness.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2024 Question 1 (Meiotic Crossing Over & Hotspots).
Rubric Requirements: Describe S phase (1 pt); Explain non-recombined chromatids (1 pt); Identify Group 1 control (1 pt); Justify mutant CTF DNA-binding role (1 pt); Identify independent variable (1 pt); Describe CTF vs IML crossing over decrease (1 pt); Predict 0 or 2 chromosome copies (1 pt); Justify nondisjunction (1 pt); Explain genetic diversity/selection (1 pt).

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1B) ===
a) The function of S phase of interphase is to replicate the DNA of the cell. Some haploid cells formed after meiosis in this experiment will only have one florescent marker because not all genes are transferred from one homologous chromosome to another in crossing over.
b) The control group for the scientists first experiment is group 1 which contains no kinetochore proteins attached to the hotspot. In the follow up experiment, the modified CTF protein that is unable to bind to DNA is the control because that is the normal effect of CTF... The independent variable is the presence or absence of unmodified and modified CTF protein in different yeast cells.
c) the frequency of crossing over is statistically significantly lower when CTF is attached compared to when IML is attached to the hotspot.
D) When CTF is attached to the hotspot, there is likely to be 2 daughter cells with 2 copies of chromosome 8, and 2 with no copies of chromosome 8. This is because with a lack of crossing over, the homologous chromosomes are going to not be separated properly during meiosis 1. Therefore nondisjunction will occur...
feedback:
Total Score: 6/9 points.
- Part (a) [1/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for describing S phase function as DNA replication. Missed (a)(ii) because stating 'not all genes are transferred' fails to clarify that the non-recombined sister chromatid was passed to the daughter cell.
- Part (b) [2/3 pts]: Earned (b)(i) for identifying Group 1 control and (b)(iii) for identifying the independent variable. Missed (b)(ii) because it failed to justify that the mutant CTF determines whether physical DNA binding is required to inhibit crossing over.
- Part (c) [1/1 pt]: Correctly described lower crossing over frequency under CTF attachment.
- Part (d) [2/3 pts]: Earned (d)(i) for predicting 2 copies / 0 copies of chromosome 8 and (d)(ii) for justifying nondisjunction due to lack of crossing over. Missed (d)(iii) due to omitting response for hotspot evolutionary advantages.

Exam: AP Biology 2024 Question 1 (Meiotic Crossing Over & Hotspots).
Rubric Requirements: Describe S phase (1 pt); Explain non-recombined chromatids (1 pt); Identify Group 1 control (1 pt); Justify mutant CTF DNA-binding role (1 pt); Identify independent variable (1 pt); Describe CTF vs IML crossing over decrease (1 pt); Predict 0 or 2 chromosome copies (1 pt); Justify nondisjunction (1 pt); Explain genetic diversity/selection (1 pt).

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1C) ===
a)i) the function of the S phase of interphase is for DNA replication. ii) Some haploid cells will only have one fluorescent marker because during crossing over the gene encoding RFP, one of them crossed over to the other chromosome.
b)i) the control group is the group of yeast cells that contained no kinetochore proteins attached to the hotspot. So group 1. ii) they used a modified CTF protein that can't bind to DNA as a control so no crossing over would occur. iii) the independent variable is the frequency of crossing over.
c) When CTF is attached to the hotspot there is less frequency of crossing over than when IML is attached to the hotspot.
d)i) If CTF is attached to the hotspot then there will be more Chromosome 8 copies. ii) Reasoning to this would be the graph showing that when there is no extra proteins attached in group 1, there is a higher frequency of crossing over. iii) the presence of hotspots could increase the populations survival rate because the hotspots allow for more crossing over meaning more genetic variation to survive.
feedback:
Total Score: 3/9 points.
- Part (a) [1/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for describing S phase DNA replication. Missed (a)(ii) due to incorrect meiotic tracking.
- Part (b) [1/3 pts]: Earned 1 pt for identifying Group 1 as control. Missed (b)(ii) for false claim that no crossing over would occur, and missed (b)(iii) by incorrectly identifying 'frequency of crossing over' (dependent variable) as the independent variable.
- Part (c) [1/1 pt]: Earned 1 pt for correctly describing lower crossing over frequency with CTF.
- Part (d) [0/3 pts]: Failed all 3 points in (d). Incorrectly predicted 'more copies', failed nondisjunction reasoning, and gave incomplete reasoning in (d)(iii) regarding how variation translates to differential survival under selection.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2024 Question 2 (9 points total).
Topic: Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results with Graphing (Temperature Effects on Toad Metabolism & ATP Synthase Inhibition).
Experimental Setup: Toad liver cells incubated at 20°C, 25°C, and 30°C to measure O2 consumption rate and ATP synthesis rate. Follow-up uses oligomycin to block ATP synthase channel protein.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) Describe water's role in ATP hydrolysis as being added to cleave/split the terminal phosphate bond.
- Part (b): (4 pts total) Bar graph construction (1 pt); Appropriate axis labels with full units [nmol/min/mg of mitochondrial protein] (1 pt); Accurate plotting of data points and +/-2SEX error bars (1 pt); Determine 30°C as temperature differing from 25°C (1 pt).
- Part (c): (1 pt) Describe positive/direct relationship between temperature and ATP synthesis; (1 pt) Calculate total O2 consumed [16.5 nmol/min/mg * 10 mg * 10 min = 1,650 nmol].
- Part (d): (1 pt) Predict proton gradient will increase / become steeper; (1 pt) Reason that ETC pumps H+ into intermembrane space while blocked ATP synthase prevents H+ flow back into matrix.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 2A) ===
a. Water dephosphorylates ATP in hydrolysis, making it ADP and breaking it apart.
b. [Bar graph drawn with clear labels, complete units, and error bars]. ii. 30°C bc error bars don't overlap.
c. i. As the temperature increases, the ATP synthesis in liver cells from toads also increases. There is a positive and direct relationship. ii. 16.5 nmol/min/mg * 10 mg * 10 min = 1650 nmol for 10 mg after 10 min.
d. i. Using oligomycin will cause the proton gradient to be uneven, with more protons in the intermembrane space and less in the matrix. ii. This is because as cellular respiration occurs, the electron transport chain pushes protons out of the mitochondrial matrix into the intermembrane space. Then an electrochemical proton gradient is established, and ATP synthase pumps protons back in... But oligomycin blocks ATP synthase from bringing protons back in, causing the uneven gradient created by the electron transport chain to remain.
feedback:
Total Score: 9/9 points (Perfect Score).
- Part (a) [1/1 pt]: Correctly described water's role in dephosphorylating/cleaving ATP.
- Part (b) [4/4 pts]: Earned all 4 points for constructing a valid bar graph, including complete axis units ('nmol/min/mg of mitochondrial protein'), accurately plotting data points and error bars, and identifying 30°C as statistically distinct.
- Part (c) [2/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for describing the positive direct trend and 1 pt for correctly calculating 1,650 nmol total O2 consumed.
- Part (d) [2/2 pts]: Earned 2 pts. Correctly predicted an increased/uneven proton gradient with accumulated H+ in the intermembrane space, and justified that ETC pumping continues while oligomycin blocks ATP synthase reentry.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2024 Question 3 (4 points total).
Topic: Scientific Investigation (Membrane Transport & Aging in Red Blood Cells).
Experimental Setup: Guinea pig RBCs ranging from 1 day to 7 months old incubated in radioactive glucose.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) Describe active transport as requiring ATP/energy (or moving low to high concentration) while passive transport does not.
- Part (b): (1 pt) Justify equal cell count control to eliminate cell density as a variable affecting glucose measurements.
- Part (c): (1 pt) Predict that internal radioactive glucose levels decrease as age increases.
- Part (d): (1 pt) Justify that lower transporter gene expression leads to fewer glucose transporters in the membrane, reducing uptake.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 3A) ===
a) Passive Transport does not require the use of energy (ATP), while active transport does require ATP.
b) The scientists used an equal number of red blood cells in each culture dish to ensure that the amount of glucose taken up by the cells was not affected by the number of blood cells and only by the age of the guinea pig.
c) As age increases, there is less radioactively labeled glucose present inside the cell.
d) Since there are less glucose transporters because expression of its gene decreases with age, less glucose can be transported into the cell.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2025 Question 1 (9 points total).
Topic: Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results (Protein Transport to the ER & siRNA Knockdowns).
Biological Context: ER transport occurs during translation (requires ER protein SR) or after translation (requires ER protein Sec62). siRNAs used to knockdown SR or Sec62 to measure effects on transport of Proteins 1, 2, and 3.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A: (1 pt) Describe ribosome function as synthesizing polypeptides/proteins or performing translation.
- Part B: (i) (1 pt) Identify dependent variable in Fig 1 as relative protein content; (ii) (1 pt) Justify Sec62 siRNA control to verify if Sec62 siRNA specifically reduces Sec62 only vs both proteins; (iii) (1 pt) Describe SR protein production increases when treated with Sec62 siRNA.
- Part C: (i) (1 pt) Identify independent variable in Fig 2 as type of siRNA or protein measured; (ii) (1 pt) Identify Proteins 2 and 3 as having increased transport under Sec62 siRNA; (iii) (1 pt) Calculate amino acid difference [(495/3) - (234/3) = 87 amino acids].
- Part D: (i) (1 pt) Support claim that Protein 1 is transported post-translationally by stating only Protein 1 showed reduced transport under Sec62 siRNA; (ii) (1 pt) Justify N-terminal transport by stating N-terminus amino acids with similar polarity or opposite charge to channel lining pass more easily.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1A) ===
a) ribosomes aid in protein synthesis, specifically in the translation stage of gene expression. The ribosome is the organelle that facilitates the creation of a polypeptide chain
b) i) dependent variable was the relative protein content (% of control)
ii) a control was included to have results to compare that of the experimented groups do. since the control models show the normal conditions would be, it allows researchers to see what changed in the experimental groups
iii) the production of the SR protein when treated with sec62 siRNA increased dramatically
c) i) the independent variable was the kind of siRNA used to treat the protein
ii) protein 2 and protein 3
iii) protein 1 nucleotides=234, amino acids=234/3=78. protein 2 nucleotides=495, amino acids=495/3=165. 165-78=87. proteins 1 and 2 have a difference in the number of amino acids of 87 amino acids.
d) i) Sec62 is needed for transportation after translation. If a protein is mostly transported after translation then it will require use of sec62. However, if the cell is treated with siRNA sec62, which reduced expression of sec62, a reduced amount of protein will be able to be transported, since sec62 is needed. according to Figure 2, of the 3 proteins, protein 1 is the only one that reduces in response to siRNA sec62, signifying that it needs Sec62, which means it is the only one that gets transported after translation.
ii) membranes are typically made of phospholipids, which require molecules to be nonpolar and uncharged while passing through. because those around the amino terminus come into contact with the membrane, those amino acids should be non-polar.
feedback:
Total Score: 7/9 points.
- Part A [1/1 pt]: Correctly described ribosome function as synthesizing proteins/polypeptides.
- Part B [2/3 pts]: Earned B(i) for relative protein content and B(iii) for stating SR protein production increased. Missed B(ii) because the control justification was vague ('to have results to compare') without specifying checking whether Sec62 siRNA selectively affected Sec62 protein alone.
- Part C [3/3 pts]: Earned all 3 pts: identified siRNA type as independent variable, listed Proteins 2 and 3, and calculated 87 amino acids.
- Part D [1/2 pts]: Earned D(i) by identifying that only Protein 1 decreased in response to Sec62 siRNA. Missed D(ii) for erroneously referencing phospholipid bilayer properties rather than polarity/charge interactions with the interior of the protein channel.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Biology 2025 Question 2 (9 points total).
Topic: Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results with Graphing (20E Pheromone Pathway & DopEcR Receptor in Moths).
Biological Setup: Male moth behavior regulated by extracellular 20E binding to GPCR DopEcR. Knockdown via siRNAs evaluated for General Activity (% total time) and Oriented Activity (% general activity time toward pheromone).
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A: (1 pt) Describe portion of receptor inside plasma membrane as nonpolar / hydrophobic.
- Part B: (i) (3 pts total) Bar graph representation (1 pt), accurate data and error bars (1 pt), appropriate axis labels with key (1 pt); (ii) (1 pt) Determine Oriented Activity as affected by DopEcR inhibition.
- Part C: (i) (1 pt) Identify control / saline-injected group as having oriented activity > 50%; (ii) (1 pt) Predict mutation preventing GTP from displacing GDP decreases oriented activity.
- Part D: (i) (1 pt) Support claim by stating increased DopEcR expression increases oriented activity / sensitivity to female pheromones; (ii) (1 pt) Explain pathway inhibitor reduces oriented activity/mating, decreasing moth population and crop damage.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 2A) ===
A) The portion of the receptor that is inside the membrane is nonpolar, causing it to be hydrophobic
B)(i) [Bar graph plotted with full labels, key, and error bars]. (ii) Oriented activity was affected by inhibiting the expression of the DopEcR receptor.
C) i) The male moths injected with saline (control solution) had oriented activity greater than 50% of general activity. ii) The mutation prevents activation of the G-protein. This decreased expression of genes associated with oriented activity in male moths. The mutation decreases oriented activity in male moths exposed to the pheromone.
D) i) Increase in gene expression of DopEcR means more of this GPCR, G protein coupled receptor, which 20E binds to in order to activate a signaling pathway. This signaling pathway ultimately increases expression of genes associated with oriented activity. So more DopEcR increases oriented activity, which is movement towards area of high pheromone concentration. Females release these pheromones to find mates, so increased oriented activity in males means they move towards females to mate.
ii) Inhibiting the DopEcR pathway prevents expression of genes associated with oriented activity in male moths. Less oriented activity means less mating, so less offspring. Less moths means less crop damage.
feedback:
Total Score: 9/9 points (Perfect Score).
- Part A [1/1 pt]: Correctly described intramembrane receptor portion as nonpolar/hydrophobic.
- Part B [4/4 pts]: Earned all 4 points. Plotted a proper bar graph with accurate error bars, full axis labels and key, and correctly identified 'oriented activity'.
- Part C [2/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for saline control group and 1 pt for predicting decreased oriented activity.
- Part D [2/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for supporting claim via increased oriented activity/female finding, and 1 pt for explaining crop protection via reduced mating/offspring.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Chemistry 2023 Question 1 (10 points total).
Topic: Manganese Compounds, Empirical Formula & Alkaline Battery Electrochemistry.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a)(i): (1 pt) Ground-state electron configuration of Mn: [Ar] 4s2 3d5 or 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2 3d5.
- Part (a)(ii): (1 pt) Identify subshell losing electrons first when forming cations: 4s.
- Part (b): (1 pt) Calculate mass of Cl in dry MnxCly: 62.673 g - 61.262 g = 1.411 g Cl.
- Part (c): (1 pt) Convert mass to moles of Cl: 1.411 g / 35.45 g/mol = 0.03980 mol Cl.
- Part (d): (1 pt) Empirical formula from 0.0199 mol Mn and 0.03980 mol Cl: ratio is 2:1 Cl to Mn -> MnCl2.
- Part (e): (1 pt) Less than. Splattering loss decreases the final dry mass of MnxCly, decreasing the calculated mass and moles of Cl.
- Part (f)(i): (1 pt) Balanced net ionic equation: 2 MnO2(s) + Zn(s) -> Mn2O3(s) + ZnO(s).
- Part (f)(ii): (1 pt) Calculate E°cell: 0.15 V - (-1.28 V) = 1.43 V.
- Part (f)(iii): (1 pt) Calculate ΔG°: -nFE° = -(2 mol e-)(96,485 C/mol)(1.43 V)(1 kJ/1000 J) = -276 kJ/molrxn.
- Part (f)(iv): (1 pt) Disagree. Sealed/enclosed battery with all solid reactants and products maintains constant total mass.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1A) ===
(a)(i) [Ar] 4s2 3d5 (ii) 4s
(b) 62.673g - 61.262g = 1.411g
(c) 1.411 g Cl * (1 mol Cl / 35.45 g Cl) = 0.03980 moles Cl = 4.0 * 10^-2 moles Cl
(d) y = 0.0398 / 0.0199 = 2.0; x = 0.0199 / 0.0199 = 1 -> MnCl2
(e) The number of moles of Cl would be less than the number of moles calculated in part (c) because the final mass of the beaker and MnxCly would be lower.
(f)(i) 2 MnO2(s) + Zn(s) -> Mn2O3(s) + ZnO(s)
(ii) E° = 0.15V + 1.28V = 1.43V
(iii) ΔG° = -(2 mol e-)(96485 C/mol e-)(1.43V) = -275947 J = -276 kJ/mol
(iv) I disagree with this claim because the cathode gains mass while the anode loses mass, so the total mass stays the same. The mass lost by the anode cannot disappear by the Law of Conservation of Mass.
feedback:
Total Score: 10/10 points (Perfect Score).
- Part (a) [2/2 pts]: Earned (a)(i) for correct ground-state configuration and (a)(ii) for identifying the 4s subshell.
- Parts (b-e) [4/4 pts]: Earned all calculation points (1.411 g Cl, 0.03980 mol Cl, MnCl2) and correctly reasoned that splattering lowers final mass and calculated moles of Cl.
- Part (f) [4/4 pts]: Earned all 4 points for balanced net ionic equation, standard cell potential (1.43 V), Gibbs free energy calculation (-276 kJ/mol), and conservation of mass justification in a closed battery system.

Exam: AP Chemistry 2023 Question 2 (10 points total).
Topic: Aluminum Chloride Thermodynamics, Potential Energy Curves, VSEPR & Gas Equilibrium.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) 1.25 mol AlCl3 * (3 mol Cl / 1 mol AlCl3) * (35.45 g Cl / 1 mol Cl) = 133 g Cl (3 sig figs).
- Part (b): (2 pts total) (1 pt) Reverse Rxn 2 (ΔH = +583 kJ) or multiply Rxn 4 by 3/2 (ΔH = +365 kJ); (1 pt) ΔH°rxn = +583 + 326 + 365 = 1274 kJ/molrxn.
- Part (c)(i): (1 pt) Cl2 bond length: 200 pm (+/- 10 pm).
- Part (c)(ii): (2 pts total) (1 pt) Minimum at internuclear distance 220 pm (+/- 10 pm); (1 pt) Minimum energy value at -425 kJ/mol (+/- 20 kJ/mol) approaching zero at 500 pm.
- Part (d)(i): (1 pt) Diagram 2 eliminated: Al has 4 electron domains (trigonal pyramidal, not trigonal planar).
- Part (d)(ii): (1 pt) Diagram 1 is best: all atoms have a formal charge of zero.
- Part (e): (1 pt) Kp = (P_Al2Cl6) / (P_AlCl3)^2.
- Part (f): (1 pt) Partial pressures: P_Al2Cl6 = (3/10)*22.1 = 6.63 atm, P_AlCl3 = (7/10)*22.1 = 15.47 atm -> Kp = 6.63 / (15.47)^2 = 0.0277.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 2A) ===
(a) 1.25 mol AlCl3 * (3 mol Cl / 1 mol AlCl3) * (35.45 g Cl / 1 mol Cl) = 133 g Cl
(b) AlCl3(g) -> Al(s) + 3/2 Cl2(g) (+583); Al(s) -> Al(g) (+326); 3/2 Cl2(g) -> 3 Cl(g) (+364.5). ΔH°1 = 1274 kJ/molrxn
(c)(i) 200 picometers (ii) [Curve plotted with minimum at (220 pm, -425 kJ/mol) approaching 0]
(d)(i) Diagram 2 can be eliminated because it has a molecular geometry of trigonal pyramidal. The central Al has three bonds and a lone pair, so it cannot be trigonal planar.
(ii) Diagram 1 is best because all atoms have a formal charge of 0.
(e) Kp = P_Al2Cl6 / (P_AlCl3)^2
(f) P_Al2Cl6 = 3/10 * 22.1 = 6.63 atm; P_AlCl3 = 7/10 * 22.1 = 15.47 atm. Kp = 6.63 / (15.47)^2 = 0.0277

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Chemistry 2023 Question 3 (10 points total).
Topic: Kinetics and Thermodynamics of Calcium Carbonate & Hydrochloric Acid Reaction.
Reaction: CaCO3(s) + 2 H+(aq) -> Ca2+(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l).
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) Net ionic equation: CaCO3(s) + 2 H+(aq) -> Ca2+(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l).
- Part (b): (1 pt) Explain Trial 5 inconsistency: 3.00 M HCl with small chunks had longer time (227 s) than 1.00 M with small chunks (112 s) or 3.00 M with large chunks (114 s).
- Part (c): (2 pts total) (1 pt) State small chunks (Trial 2) have greater surface area than large chunk (Trial 3); (1 pt) Greater surface area causes more frequent/effective particle collisions.
- Part (d): (1 pt) Disagree with zero-order claim: Tripling [HCl] decreases reaction time by 1/3 (triples rate), indicating first order (or changing [HCl] changes rate).
- Part (e): (2 pts total) (1 pt) Moles HCl reacted = 1.00 g CaCO3 * (1 mol/100.09 g) * (2 mol HCl / 1 mol CaCO3) = 0.0200 mol; (1 pt) [HCl] remaining = (0.0500 mol - 0.0200 mol) / 0.0500 L = 0.600 M.
- Part (f): (1 pt) Exothermic because solution temperature increases.
- Part (g)(i): (1 pt) q = mcΔT = (51.0 g)(4.0 J/g°C)(21.90°C - 21.20°C) = 140 J.
- Part (g)(ii): (1 pt) ΔH°rxn = -q / mol CaCO3 = -0.14 kJ / 0.00999 mol = -14 kJ/molrxn.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 3A) ===
(a) CaCO3(s) + 2 H+(aq) -> Ca2+(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l)
(b) The student's claim is correct because the time of reaction for small chunks should be between that of fine powder and large chunks... in Trial 5 reaction time was 227s, which is greater than other trials with [HCl] = 3.0M...
(c) The smaller particle size of Trial 2 increases the surface area of the CaCO3, thus increasing the number of CaCO3 exposed to collisions with HCl particles and increasing the reaction rate for Trial 2 as more effective collisions can occur at a time...
(d) I disagree. Comparing Trials 1 and 3 with Trials 4 and 6 shows that at three times the concentration of HCl, the reaction time went down by a factor of three. This relationship implies a first-order kinetics...
(e) 1.00g CaCO3 * (1 mol CaCO3 / 100.09 g) * (2 mol HCl / 1 mol CaCO3) = 0.0200 mol HCl reacted. Initial = 0.0500 moles. Remaining = 0.0300 moles HCl / 0.0500 L = 0.600 M HCl
(f) The reaction is exothermic... temperature increased and since the solution is the surroundings, heat was released from the reaction and absorbed by surroundings.
(g)(i) q = mcΔT = (51.0g)(4.0 J/g°C)(21.90°C - 21.20°C) = 140 J
(ii) qrxn = -qsolution = -140 J. ΔHrxn = -0.14 kJ / (1.00g / 100.09 g/mol) = -14 kJ/molrxn
feedback:
Total Score: 10/10 points (Perfect Score).
- Part (a) [1/1 pt]: Correctly balanced net ionic equation.
- Part (b) [1/1 pt]: Valid explanation of Trial 5 inconsistency using table trends.
- Part (c) [2/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for surface area relationship and 1 pt for collision frequency.
- Part (d) [1/1 pt]: Disagreed with zero-order claim and correctly proved first-order kinetics.
- Part (e) [2/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for moles of HCl consumed (0.0200 mol) and 1 pt for remaining molarity (0.600 M).
- Part (f) [1/1 pt]: Correctly classified as exothermic based on temperature rise.
- Part (g) [2/2 pts]: Earned 1 pt for q = 140 J and 1 pt for ΔH° = -14 kJ/molrxn.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Chemistry 2024 Question 2 (10 points total).
Topic: Long Answer (Maleic Acid & Sodium Bicarbonate Reaction, Gas Stoichiometry, Kinetics, Entropy & Diprotic Buffer).
Reaction: H2C4H2O4(aq) + 2 NaHCO3(aq) -> 2 CO2(g) + 2 H2O(l) + Na2C4H2O4(aq).
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a)(i): (1 pt) 0.0114 mol CO2 * 44.01 g/mol = 0.502 g CO2.
- Part (a)(ii): (1 pt) V = nRT/P = (0.0114 mol)(0.08206 L*atm/mol*K)(293 K) / 1.25 atm = 0.219 L.
- Part (b)(i): (1 pt) Surface area increases upon grinding into powder.
- Part (b)(ii): (1 pt) Shorter than. Powder has larger surface area -> more frequent collisions between water and surface particles -> faster dissolution rate.
- Part (b)(iii): (1 pt) Equal to. Same initial reactant moles produce the same moles and volume of CO2(g) under identical conditions.
- Part (c): (1 pt) NaHCO3 is limiting reactant because increasing NaHCO3 in Trial 4 increases CO2 produced (or theoretical yield calculation shows NaHCO3 produces fewer moles of CO2: 0.01489 mol vs 0.02659 mol).
- Part (d): (1 pt) ΔS° > 0 because aqueous reactants produce 2 moles of gas (CO2). Gases have much higher microstates/dispersal.
- Part (e): (1 pt) Disagree. Endothermic (ΔH > 0) with ΔS > 0 is only thermodynamically favorable at high temperatures where TΔS > ΔH.
- Part (f): (1 pt) pKa2 = -log(8.5 * 10^-7) = 6.07.
- Part (g): (1 pt) pH = pKa + log([A2-]/[HA-]) -> [C4H2O4 2-] / [HC4H2O4 -] = 10^(7.00 - 6.07) = 8.5.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 2A) ===
(a)(i) .0114 mol CO2 * (44.01 g CO2 / 1 mol CO2) = .502 g CO2
(ii) V = nRT/P = (0.0114 mol)(0.08206)(293 K) / 1.25 atm = .219 L
(b)(i) By grinding to a powder, the surface area increases.
(ii) The time required for dissolving will be shorter in the second experiment because by increasing the surface area of the reactants, there is more area available for the reactants and water molecules to collide. This will increase the rate of collisions... and thus increase speed of dissolution.
(iii) The volume of CO2 will be the same for both experiments because the amount of CO2 produced is dependent on the molar quantities of the reactants, not the reaction rate...
(c) The limiting reactant in Trial 3 is the NaHCO3. When more NaHCO3 was added in the 4th trial, the amount of CO2 increased. Thus NaHCO3 was consumed before the H2C4H2O4...
(d) The entropy increases due to the production of gas molecules. These gas molecules have greater possible microstates, as they have greater freedom of movement than strictly dissolved particles...
(e) I disagree because the reaction is endothermic. While ΔSrxn > 0, the reaction is only thermodynamically favorable at high temperatures. Based on ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, ΔG is only negative when ΔH < TΔS...
(f) pKa2 = -log(Ka2) = -log(8.5 * 10^-7) = 6.07
(g) pH = pKa + log([CB]/[A]) -> 7.00 = 6.07 + log([C4H2O4 2-]/[HC4H2O4 -]) -> .93 = log(...) -> [C4H2O4 2-]/[HC4H2O4 -] = 8.5
feedback:
Total Score: 10/10 points (Perfect Score).
- Part (a) [2/2 pts]: Earned (a)(i) for 0.502 g CO2 and (a)(ii) for ideal gas calculation (0.219 L).
- Part (b) [3/3 pts]: Earned (b)(i) for surface area increase, (b)(ii) for collision frequency/shorter time, and (b)(iii) for equal gas volume.
- Part (c) [1/1 pt]: Correctly identified NaHCO3 limiting reactant using data comparison between Trials 3 and 4.
- Part (d) [1/1 pt]: Accurately linked positive entropy to gas formation and microstates.
- Part (e) [1/1 pt]: Disagreed with favorability claim, correctly citing high-temperature requirement for endothermic reactions.
- Parts (f-g) [2/2 pts]: Earned (f) for pKa2 = 6.07 and (g) for buffer ratio = 8.5.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Chemistry 2024 Question 3 (10 points total).
Topic: Long Answer (Sterling Silver Alloy, Atomic Radius, Tarnish Stoichiometry & Rhodium Electroplating).
Reaction & Data: 2 Ag(s) + H2S(g) -> Ag2S(s) + H2(g). Plating Rh(s) from acidic Rh2(SO4)3(aq).
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) Oxidation numbers: Ag(s) = 0, Ag2S(s) = +1.
- Part (b)(i): (1 pt) Substitutional alloy because Ag and Cu have similar atomic radii (165 pm vs 145 pm).
- Part (b)(ii): (1 pt) Ag has larger radius because it occupies more principal energy levels (n=5 vs n=4 for Cu), placing valence electrons farther from nucleus with weaker Coulombic attraction.
- Part (c): (2 pts total) (1 pt) Mass Ag2S = 409.21 g - 398.94 g = 10.27 g; (1 pt) Moles Ag = 10.27 g * (1 mol Ag2S / 247.80 g) * (2 mol Ag / 1 mol Ag2S) = 0.08289 mol Ag.
- Part (d)(i): (1 pt) Balanced net ionic: 4 Rh3+(aq) + 6 H2O(l) -> 4 Rh(s) + 3 O2(g) + 12 H+(aq).
- Part (d)(ii): (1 pt) E°cell = +0.80 V - 1.23 V = -0.43 V.
- Part (d)(iii): (1 pt) Negative E°cell means the reaction is thermodynamically unfavorable (non-spontaneous), requiring an external power source.
- Part (e): (2 pts total) (1 pt) Moles e- = 2.8 g Rh * (1 mol / 102.9 g) * (3 mol e- / 1 mol Rh) = 0.082 mol e-; (1 pt) Time = 0.082 mol e- * (96485 C / 1 mol e-) * (1 s / 2.0 C) = 3900 s (2 sig figs).

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 3A) ===
(a) Ag(s) = 0, Ag2S(s) = +1
(b)(i) The atomic radius of Ag and Cu are similar in size. A substitutional alloy contains metals of similar atomic radii.
(ii) Silver contains electrons in a higher energy level (4d/5s) than copper (3d/4s). These silver's electrons are a greater distance from the nucleus than copper's and have a weaker force attracting to the nucleus (F proportional to 1/r^2 by Coulomb's Law). Thus the atomic radius of silver atoms are larger than copper.
(c) 409.21 - 398.94 = 10.27 g Ag2S. 10.27 g Ag2S * (1 mol Ag2S / 247.80 g Ag2S) * (2 mol Ag / 1 mol Ag2S) = 0.08289 mol Ag removed
(d)(i) 4 Rh3+(aq) + 6 H2O(l) -> 4 Rh(s) + 3 O2(g) + 12 H+(aq)
(ii) E°cell = E°red - E°ox = +0.80 - (+1.23) = -0.43 V
(iii) The E°cell is negative so the reaction is thermodynamically unfavorable since ΔG > 0 by ΔG = -nFE°. To make E°cell positive and favorable, external voltage must be added.
(e) 2.8 g Rh * (1 mol Rh / 102.91 g Rh) * (3 mol e- / 1 mol Rh) * (96485 C / 1 mol e-) * (1 s / 2.0 C) = 3900 s

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Chemistry 2025 Question 1 (10 points total).
Topic: Long Answer (Magnesium Isotopes, Coulomb's Law, pH/pOH, Dilution, Ksp & Le Chatelier).
Data & Reactions: Mg-24 (79%), Mg-25, Mg-26. Ksp = [Mg2+][OH-]^2. HNO3 addition to Mg(OH)2.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A(i): (1 pt) Draw peak heights for Mg-25 and Mg-26 between 10 and 11 relative abundance[cite: 25].
- Part A(ii): (1 pt) Mg-26 has one more neutron (14 neutrons) than Mg-25 (13 neutrons)[cite: 25].
- Part B(i): (1 pt) Na+ has a smaller charge (+1) than Mg2+ (+2), resulting in weaker Coulombic attraction to water[cite: 25].
- Part B(ii): (1 pt) Na+ is larger than Mg2+, so distance between Na+ and water oxygen is greater, decreasing Coulombic force (F proportional to 1/r^2)[cite: 25].
- Part C: (1 pt) pOH = -log(2.80 * 10^-4) = 3.553 -> pH = 14.000 - 3.553 = 10.447 (or 10.45)[cite: 25].
- Part D: (1 pt) [Mg2+] = (1.85 * 10^-3 M * 0.03500 L) / (0.03500 L + 0.05000 L) = 7.62 * 10^-4 M[cite: 25].
- Part E(i): (1 pt) Ksp = [Mg2+][OH-]^2[cite: 25].
- Part E(ii): (1 pt) Q = [Mg2+][OH-]^2 = (7.62 * 10^-4)(1.65 * 10^-4)^2 = 2.07 * 10^-11[cite: 25].
- Part E(iii): (1 pt) Precipitate forms because Q > Ksp[cite: 25].
- Part F: (1 pt) Decrease. H+ from HNO3 neutralizes OH-, decreasing [OH-] so Q < Ksp, shifting equilibrium right to dissolve more solid Mg(OH)2[cite: 25].

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1A) ===
Part A: i. [Lines drawn at relative abundance ~10.5 for 25 and 26]. ii. Both magnesium-25 and magnesium-26 have 12 protons. Magnesium-26 however has 14 neutrons while magnesium-25 has 13 neutrons. This additional neutron is responsible for the difference in mass.
Part B: i. Mg+2 has a larger charge of +2 compared to +1 for Na+1... larger charge means a larger force... Na+1 will have a weaker attraction to the partial negative charge of the O in water than Mg+2. ii. From Coulomb's Law, a larger separation means a smaller Coulombic force. Both Na+1 and Mg+2 have 10 electrons, but Na+1 has one less proton (11 vs 12) resulting in a larger ionic radius for Na+1. This larger radius results in a larger separation between Na+1 and water, resulting in a weaker attraction.
Part C: pOH = -log[OH-] = -log(2.8 * 10^-4) = 3.55. pH = 14 - pOH = 10.45
Part D: (1.85 * 10^-3 mol/L * 0.0350 L) / 0.085 L = 7.62 * 10^-4 M Mg(NO3)2 -> [Mg+2] = 7.62 * 10^-4 M
Part E: i. Ksp = [Mg+2][OH-]^2. ii. Q = (7.62 * 10^-4)(1.65 * 10^-4)^2 = 2.07 * 10^-11. iii. Since Q > K, the reaction will shift left to approach equilibrium, producing Mg(OH)2(s). So yes, a precipitate should form.

- Part B(i): (1 pt) [HAsc] = (0.0160 L * 0.0550 M NaOH) / 0.0100 L HAsc = 0.0880 M[cite: 26].
- Part B(ii): (1 pt) pKa = pH at half-equivalence point (8.0 mL NaOH) = 4.1 (acceptable: 4.0 - 4.3)[cite: 26].
- Part B(iii): (1 pt) [Asc-]/[HAsc] = 10^(pH - pKa) = 10^(4.7 - 4.1) = 10^0.6 = 4.0[cite: 26].
- Part C(i): (1 pt) First order with respect to HAsc because comparing Trials 1 and 3, doubling [HAsc] while [I3-] is constant doubles the rate[cite: 26].
- Part C(ii): (2 pts total) (1 pt) k = Rate / ([HAsc][I3-]) = (2.457 * 10^-4) / (0.450 * 1.200) = 4.55 * 10^-4; (1 pt) Units: M^-1 s^-1[cite: 26].

Part B: i. 16.0 mL NaOH * (1 L / 1000 mL) * (0.0550 mol NaOH / 1 L) = 8.80 * 10^-4 mol NaOH = 8.80 * 10^-4 mol HAsc. (8.80 * 10^-4 mol HAsc / 10.0 mL HAsc) * (1000 mL / 1 L) = 0.0880 M HAsc. ii. Equivalence point = 16.0 mL -> Half-equivalence point = 8.0 mL. At 8.0 mL, pH = pKa -> pKa = 4.1. iii. pH = pKa + log([Asc-]/[HAsc]) -> 4.7 = 4.1 + log(...) -> 0.6 = log(...) -> [Asc-]/[HAsc] = 10^0.6 = 4.0.
Part C: i. Using trials 1 and 3, we can see that the reaction rate is 2 times greater when [HAsc] is 2 times greater, so it is first order with respect to [HAsc]. ii. 2.457 * 10^-4 M/s = k (0.450 M)(1.200 M) -> k = 4.55 * 10^-4 s^-1 M^-1.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Chemistry 2025 Question 3 (10 points total).
Topic: Long Answer (White Phosphorus P4 Structure, Entropy, Calorimetry Enthalpy, Hess's Law & Gas Equilibrium Kp).
Reactions: P4(s) + 5 O2(g) -> P4O10(s); PCl3(g) + Cl2(g) <=> PCl5(g), ΔH°2 = -88 kJ/molrxn.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A: (1 pt) Complete P4 Lewis diagram: 1 lone pair (2 dots) on each of the 4 phosphorus atoms[cite: 27].
- Part B(i): (1 pt) ΔS° < 0 because gaseous reactants (5 O2) form a solid product; gases have far more microstates/dispersal than solids[cite: 27].
- Part B(ii): (1 pt) Yes/Correct. In ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS°, since ΔS° < 0, the -TΔS° term is positive. Thermodynamic favorability (ΔG° < 0) is driven solely by the exothermic enthalpy (ΔH° < 0)[cite: 27].
- Part C(i): (1 pt) q = mcΔT = (100.1 g)(4.18 J/g°C)(22.38°C - 22.00°C) = 160 J = 0.16 kJ (2 sig figs)[cite: 27].
- Part C(ii): (2 pts total) (1 pt) Magnitude: ΔH°rxn = -0.16 kJ / (0.100 g / 283.9 g/mol) = 450 kJ/molrxn; (1 pt) Sign: -450 kJ/molrxn[cite: 27].
- Part D: (1 pt) Less than. Less P4O10 means fewer moles react, releasing less thermal energy to water, causing a smaller ΔT[cite: 27].
- Part E: (1 pt) Hess's Law: ΔH°f(PCl5) = 1/4 ΔH°1 + ΔH°2 = 1/4(-1148) + (-88) = -375 kJ/mol[cite: 27].
- Part F(i): (1 pt) Kp = (P_PCl5) / (P_PCl3 * P_Cl2) = (4.00) / (2.00 * 6.00) = 0.333[cite: 27].
- Part F(ii): (1 pt) Decrease. Reaction is exothermic (ΔH° < 0), so increasing temperature shifts equilibrium toward reactants, decreasing Kp[cite: 27].

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 3A) ===
Part A: [Drew 2 lone pair electrons on each P atom in the tetrahedral P4 cage]
Part B: i. ΔS° is negative because as the reaction progresses, gas molecules are used to produce solid molecules. Solids have less entropy than gases because there are less possible locations and positions of the solid molecules compared to the gas molecules. The solid molecules also move slower. So entropy decreases and ΔS° is negative. ii. ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS°. The student is correct. A reaction is thermodynamically favorable when ΔG° is negative. Since ΔS° is negative, -TΔS° will be a positive value. The only way that the reaction can be thermodynamically favorable is if ΔH° is negative.
Part C: i. q = (100.0g + 0.100g)(4.18 J/g°C)(22.38°C - 22.00°C) = 160 J = 0.16 kJ. ii. 0.100 g P4O10 * (1 mol P4O10 / 283.9 g) = 0.000352 mol. ΔH°rxn = -0.16 kJ / 0.000352 mol = -450 kJ/molrxn.
Part D: ΔT would less than ΔT of the first trial. P4O10 is the limiting reactant... when there is less P4O10 in the calorimeter, less reactions occur, so less heat is transferred to the water. So the water experiences less change in temperature.
Part E: 1/4 P4(s) + 6/4 Cl2(g) -> PCl3(g) (1/4 * -1148); PCl3(g) + Cl2(g) <=> PCl5(g) (-88). Sum: 1/4 P4 + 5/2 Cl2 -> PCl5 -> ΔH°f = -375 kJ/molrxn.
Part F: i. Kp = P_PCl5 / (P_PCl3 * P_Cl2) = (4.00) / (2.00 * 6.00) = 0.333. ii. Kp decreases when the temperature is raised. ΔH°2 is negative, so the reaction is exothermic. When heat is added, the reaction will shift towards the reactants and produce more PCl3 and Cl2. When concentrations of PCl3 and Cl2 increase, Kp decreases.

- Part B [2/2 pts]: Earned B(i) for microstate/positional entropy explanation and B(ii) for thermodynamic enthalpy drive justification[cite: 27].

- Part D [1/1 pt]: Correctly concluded ΔT is less than due to less heat transferred[cite: 27].

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP English Language and Composition 2024 Question 3 (Set 1) (6 points total).
Topic: Argument Essay (Value of Documenting Life with Selfies - J Wortham Claim).
Prompt: In a 2013 New York Times article, J Wortham claimed selfies are best seen as 'a kind of visual diary, a way to mark our short existence and hold it up to others as proof that we were here.' Write an essay arguing your position on the extent to which Wortham's claim is valid.
Rubric Expectations:
- Row A: Thesis (0-1 pt): Responds to the prompt with a defensible position.
- Row B: Evidence & Commentary (0-4 pts): Provides specific evidence supporting all claims in a line of reasoning with clear commentary explaining how evidence supports the argument.
- Row C: Sophistication (0-1 pt): Crafts a nuanced argument, explores complexities/tensions, or employs a vivid/persuasive style.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 3A) ===
Members of older generations often ridicule younger generations for their seemingly self-absorbed obsession with 'selfies.' However, labeling these images as nothing more than expressions of narcissism and superficiality does not account for the immense value they also present. J Wortham's claim that selfies function as a 'visual diary' speaks volumes on the worth of these pictures. Documenting one's life with selfies has historical value in providing future generations with depictions of life in a certain time period, as well as sentimental value in capturing the interpersonal relationships of those in the images.
To begin, there is significant historical value in characterizing a particular time period with selfies so that future historians can gain a greater understanding of how people lived during that time... During WWII, teenager Anne Frank kept a diary about her experience hiding from Nazis, providing historians with insight about the common experiences of Jewish people... Similarly, with the Snapchat app, users capture pictures and overlay text descriptions. During historical events like the COVID-19 pandemic, teenagers, like Anne Frank, provided commentary on the frustration of mask-wearing and social distancing... These selfies will serve as primary sources in future years, perhaps being studied like Anne Frank's diary... Furthermore, selfies also contain sentimental value because of their capability to immortalize interpersonal relationships beyond the lifespans of humans...
feedback:

- Row B (Evidence & Commentary) [4/4 pts]: Earned 4 pts. Developed a strong line of reasoning comparing Anne Frank's diary to COVID-19 Snapchat selfies as historical primary sources, alongside analyzing the sentimental role of digital photo archives in preserving relationships[cite: 36].
- Row C (Sophistication) [1/1 pt]: Earned 1 pt. Demonstrated sophistication by insightfully placing selfies within the historical tradition of personal diarists rather than treating them merely as modern social media exhibitionism[cite: 36].

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 2A) ===
David Treuer, an Indian novelist who grew up on a Minnesota reservation, argues that Americans should pay more attention to Indians and put forth more effort in understanding their livelihoods. Using rhetorical techniques, Treuer does this by first comparing and contrasting reservations with non-reservation land, then describing reservations more in depth, and finally describing the importance of Indians in American history.
In order to convey his argument... Treuer begins by comparing the land most Americans are familiar with to reservation lands. He states that the sign welcoming travelers into the reservation 'is soon behind you and soon forgotten' (Treuer 2). This anaphora with the repetition of 'soon' emphasizes the fact that non-Indians entering a reservation typically ignore the fact that they have entered such a place... Continuing, Treuer states that 'The houses don't look all that different [on the reservations], perhaps a little smaller, a little more ramshackle' (2)... 'Some reservations are so small that the sign itself seems larger than the land it denotes' (3). This hyperbole emphasizes the difference in sizes... Treuer establishes his argument by expressing the importance of Indians in American history. He states that 'The Oneida were allies of the Revolutionary Army who fed U.S. troops at Valley Forge and helped defeat the British in New York' (Treuer 4)... Treuer also uses personification, stating that 'Indians are part of the story that America tells itself' (5)...

Amanda Gorman's statement is a reflection of the dichotomy of pessimism and optimism as less of a relationship between two diametrically opposed viewpoints, but instead, two sides of the same coin of situational and worldwide awareness... Despite these somber and depressing conditions, the idea of 'the coast' that is referenced throughout the book, as the driving force of the two character's travel provides the idea that in times of strife, there is always a light in the darkness to cling to... The relationship between pessimism and optimism is typically represented as having a 'glass half full' vs 'glass half empty' mindset... During times of economic recession or even depression, it is not uncommon for people to focus on how these set backs may negatively affect their well being... This recognition of one's woes is often still paired with an assurance that things will get better...

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Statistics 2024 Question 1 (4 points total).
Topic: Focus on Inference (Two-Sample z-Test for a Difference in Population Proportions).
Problem Context: An exercise center investigates whether the proportion of younger members (ages 18-55, sample n1 = 170, 51 interested) and older members (ages 56+, sample n2 = 230, 79 interested) who want online fitness classes differs significantly at alpha = 0.05.
Rubric Expectations:
- Section 1 (Hypotheses & Identification): (1) Identify two-sample z-test for difference in proportions; (2) State H0: pyounger = polder vs. Ha: pyounger != polder; (3) Define parameters in context with population terms ('all', 'true proportion'). [Scored E/P/I]
- Section 2 (Conditions & Mechanics): (1) Verify independent random samples & 10% condition (170 < 10% of younger members, 230 < 10% of older members); (2) Large count check using pooled p_hat = 0.325 (170*0.325 = 55.25 >= 10, 170*0.675 = 114.75 >= 10, 230*0.325 = 74.75 >= 10, 230*0.675 = 155.25 >= 10); (3) Calculate z-statistic = -0.918 (or 0.918); (4) Calculate p-value = 0.359. [Scored E/P/I]
- Section 3 (Conclusion): (1) Compare p-value (0.359) > alpha (0.05) and state decision to fail to reject H0; (2) State non-definitive conclusion in context regarding lack of convincing statistical evidence of a difference. [Scored E/P/I]

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1A) ===
2 sample z test for a difference in proportions
Ho: p1 = p2; Ha: p1 != p2, where p1 represents the proportion of all exercise center members ages 18 to 55 years who would be interested in taking online fitness classes and p2 represents the proportion of all exercise center members ages 56 years and older who would be interested in taking online fitness classes.
Conditions: 1) random - question states random sample of 170 members ages 18 to 55 was selected and random sample of 230 members age 56 years and older was selected. 2) independent - n1 = 170 <= 10% N (reasonable to assume over 1700 members), n2 = 230 <= 10% N (reasonable to assume over 2300 members). 3) normal - pc = (51+79)/(170+230) = .325; n1*pc = 170(.325) = 55.25 >= 10; n1(1-pc) = 170(.675) = 114.75 >= 10; n2*pc = 230(.325) = 74.75 >= 10; n2(1-pc) = 230(.675) = 155.25 >= 10.
Calculations: z = -0.9177765491; p = .3587357818.
Because the p value of .36 > alpha = 0.05, we fail to reject Ho. There is not convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all exercise center members ages 18-55 who would take online fitness classes differs from the proportion of all center members 56+ who would take online fitness class.
feedback:
Total Score: 4/4 points (Complete Response: Section 1 - E, Section 2 - E, Section 3 - E)[cite: 43].
- Section 1 [E]: Correctly named the two-sample z-test, stated two-sided hypotheses, and clearly defined parameters in context with population descriptor 'all'[cite: 43].
- Section 2 [E]: Checked random sampling, verified both 10% conditions, executed the large counts condition with pooled proportions, and reported accurate test statistic (z = -0.918) and p-value (0.359)[cite: 43].
- Section 3 [E]: Correctly compared p-value to alpha, made the appropriate decision (fail to reject H0), and framed the non-definitive conclusion in full context[cite: 43].

Problem Context: An elementary school sold bottles in 3 sizes: small (0.5), medium (0.3), large (0.2). A middle school sold 3 times as many bottles total, with equal proportions (1/3 each) across sizes. High School A and B bottle sales are shown in a mosaic plot.

- Part (c): (i) (1 pt) State High School A sold a greater proportion of large bottles based on height/relative frequency (0.7 > 0.6); (ii) (1 pt) State High School B sold a greater number of large bottles because the area of the rectangle representing large bottles for High School B is larger than that for High School A. === QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Statistics 2024 Question 3 (4 points total).
Topic: Focus on Sampling and Experimental Design (Observational Studies, Randomized Assignment & Scope of Inference).
Problem Context: Researchers ask car owners to estimate gas mileage across 4 models (A, B, C, D). James wants to test if autopilot on Model D improves mileage over 70 commute days. He then wants to generalize findings to his Model D club.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (1 pt) Observational study; (1 pt) No treatments were imposed / no random assignment of car models; (1 pt) Context ('car owners', 'models'). [Scored E/P/I]
- Part (b): (1 pt) Label 70 days (1 to 70); (1 pt) Implement random process where all assignments are equally likely (random number generator 1-70 without repeats or 70 slips of paper mixed well in a bag); (1 pt) Exactly 35 days assigned to autopilot and remaining 35 days to no autopilot. [Scored E/P/I]
- Part (c): (1 pt) Sample more cars/members; (1 pt) Use random sampling from the population of interest; (1 pt) Context (Model D cars/owners in his club). [Scored E/P/I]

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 3A) ===
(a) Observational study. There are no treatments that are randomly being assigned to subjects. The researchers are only asking car owners of each model for an estimate of their mileage.
(b) Number each of the 70 days with a number 1-70, inclusive. Use a random number generator to pick 35 numbers between 1 and 70 without replacement. 35 numbers picked will correspond to a day. The 35 days selected will be assigned the treatment of driving using autopilot feature and the remaining days will be assigned the treatment of driving without autopilot feature.
(c) James would need to replicate his study to a random sample of Model D owners in the club to be able to generalize the results to all Model D cars in the club.
feedback:
Total Score: 4/4 points (Complete Response: Part (a) - E, Part (b) - E, Part (c) - E)[cite: 45].
- Part (a) [E]: Correctly identified observational study, justified by lack of assigned treatments, with full car owner context[cite: 45].
- Part (b) [E]: Labeled days 1-70, used a random number generator without replacement, and allocated exactly 35 days to autopilot and 35 to no autopilot[cite: 45].
- Part (c) [E]: Stated need for a random sample of multiple Model D owners from the club[cite: 45].

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Statistics 2024 Question 4 (4 points total).
Topic: Focus on Probability and Sampling Distributions (Geometric Distribution & Expected Value of Discrete Variable).
Problem Context: In a game, opening a geode yields a red crystal with probability p = 0.08. Sarah opens geodes until finding a red crystal (G ~ Geom(0.08)). Conrad opens geodes until finding a red crystal or until 4 geodes are opened (random variable Y = {1, 2, 3, 4}).
Rubric Expectations:
- Part (a): (i) Mean of G = 1/p = 1/0.08 = 12.5 geodes; (ii) Standard deviation of G = sqrt(1-p)/p = sqrt(0.92)/0.08 = 11.99 geodes (or 12). [Needs 3 of 4 components for E]
- Part (b): (i) P(Y = 3) = (0.92)^2 * (0.08) = 0.067712; (ii) P(Y = 4) = 1 - [P(1)+P(2)+P(3)] = 1 - [0.08 + 0.0736 + 0.067712] = 0.778688 (or (0.92)^4 + (0.92)^3*(0.08)). [Needs 3 of 4 components for E]
- Part (c): (i) E(Y) = 1(0.08) + 2(0.0736) + 3(0.067712) + 4(0.778688) = 3.545 geodes; (ii) Interpret E(Y): The average number of geodes opened across many, many repeated trials of this game. [Needs E(Y) calc + work + long-run average interpretation in context for E]

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 4A) ===
(a)(i) The distribution is geometric with p = .08 because Sarah is opening geodes until a red crystal is found. The mean of the distribution is 1/p = 1/.08 = 12.5 geodes.
(ii) standard deviation of number of geodes Sarah opens until a red crystal is found is sqrt(1-p)/p = sqrt(1-.08)/.08 = 11.99 geodes. Distribution is geometric with p = .08.
(b)(i) P(Y=3) = (1-p)^(x-1) * p = (1-.08)^(3-1) * (.08) = 0.067712. There is a 0.067712 probability that Conrad will open three geodes.
(ii) P(Y=4) = 1 - P(Y <= 3) = 1 - .08 - .0736 - .067712 = 0.778688. There is a 0.778688 probability that Conrad will open four geodes.
(c)(i) mu_Y = (1)(.08) + (2)(.0736) + 3(.067712) + 4(.778688) = 3.545088 geodes.
(ii) On average, Conrad will open 3.545088 geodes if he stops opening geodes after finding a red crystal or when 4 geodes have been opened. If Conrad plays the game this way many, many times, the average number of geodes he will open will approximate 3.545088 geodes.
feedback:
Total Score: 4/4 points (Complete Response: Part (a) - E, Part (b) - E, Part (c) - E)[cite: 46].
- Part (a) [E]: Correctly calculated mean (12.5) and standard deviation (11.99) with full geometric formulas shown[cite: 46].
- Part (b) [E]: Correctly computed P(Y=3) = 0.067712 and P(Y=4) = 0.778688 with complete supporting work[cite: 46].
- Part (c) [E]: Calculated expected value E(Y) = 3.545 geodes showing all terms, and provided a textbook long-run average interpretation ('many, many times') in context[cite: 46].

(ii) The mean is the expected value of the number of geodes Conrad will open

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Calculus AB 2025 Question 3 (9 points total - No Calculator).
Topic: Tabular Rates, Derivative Approximation, IVT, Trapezoidal Sum & Definite Integral.
Table Data: Reading rate R(t) in words/min at t = 0 (90), t = 2 (100), t = 8 (150), t = 10 (162). Teacher rate: W(t) = -(3/10)t^2 + 8t + 100.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A: (P1) Difference quotient: (R(2) - R(0))/(2 - 0) = (100 - 90)/2 = 5; (P2) Units: words/min^2 (or words per minute per minute).
- Part B: (P3) State R is continuous because R is differentiable; (P4) IVT justification: R(0) = 90 < 155 < 162 = R(10), so by IVT there exists c in (0, 10) such that R(c) = 155.
- Part C: (P5) Trapezoidal sum form: (2-0)(90+100)/2 + (8-2)(100+150)/2 + (10-8)(150+162)/2; (P6) Value: 190 + 750 + 312 = 1252.
- Part D: (P7) Integral setup: int_0^10 W(t) dt; (P8) Antiderivative: -(1/10)t^3 + 4t^2 + 100t; (P9) Evaluate: -(1/10)(1000) + 4(100) + 100(10) - 0 = 1300 words.

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Calculus AB 2025 Question 5 (9 points total - No Calculator).
Topic: Particle Kinematics along x-axis, Velocity, Opposite Direction Intervals, Speed & Position Integration.
Given: Particle H position x_H(t) = e^(t^2 - 4t); Particle J velocity v_J(t) = 2t(t^2 - 1)^3. Particle J initial position x_J(0) = 7.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A: (P1) Differentiate x_H(t): v_H(t) = (2t - 4)e^(t^2 - 4t); (P2) v_H(1) = -2e^-3.
- Part B: (P3) Set v_H(t) = 0 (t = 2) and v_J(t) = 0 (t = 1); (P4) Sign analysis: H moves left on (0, 2) and right on (2, 5); J moves left on (0, 1) and right on (1, 5); (P5) Conclusion: Particles move in opposite directions on (1, 2).
- Part C: (P6) Speed of J at t = 2 is increasing because v_J(2) > 0 and v'_J(2) > 0 (velocity and acceleration share the same sign).
- Part D: (P7) Position integral setup: x_J(2) = 7 + int_0^2 2t(t^2 - 1)^3 dt; (P8) Antiderivative: (1/4)(t^2 - 1)^4; (P9) Value: 7 + (1/4)[(3)^4 - (-1)^4] = 7 + (1/4)(80) = 27.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 5A) ===
Part A: x_H(t) = e^(t^2 - 4t) -> v_H(t) = (2t - 4)e^(t^2 - 4t) -> v_H(1) = (2(1) - 4)e^(1 - 4) = -2e^-3
Part B: v_H(t) = (2t - 4)e^(t^2 - 4t) = 0 -> t = 2. H moves left from 0 to 2, right from 2 to 5. v_J(t) = 2t(t^2 - 1)^3 = 0 -> t = 0, 1, -1. J moves left from 0 to 1, right from 1 to 5. H and J move in opposite directions from 1 < t < 2; they have opposite sign velocity on this interval.
Part C: v_J(2) = 2(2)(2^2 - 1)^3 = 4(3)^3 > 0. v_J'(2) > 0. Since velocity and acceleration have the same sign, the particle is speeding up at t = 2.
Part D: x_J(t) = int v_J(t) dt = int 2t(t^2 - 1)^3 dt = int 2t(t^6 - 3t^4 + 3t^2 - 1) dt = int (2t^7 - 6t^5 + 6t^3 - 2t) dt = (1/4)t^8 - t^6 + (3/2)t^4 - t^2 + C. 7 = 0 + C -> C = 7. x_J(2) = (1/4)(2)^8 - (2)^6 + (3/2)(2)^4 - (2)^2 + 7 = 64 - 64 + 24 - 4 + 7 = 27
feedback:
Total Score: 9/9 points (Perfect Score: 1-1-1-1-1-1-1-1-1)[cite: 51].
- Part A [2/2 pts]: Earned P1 for chain rule derivative and P2 for -2e^-3[cite: 51].
- Part B [3/3 pts]: Earned P3 for critical points (t=2, t=1), P4 for directional analysis on (0, 5), and P5 for opposite direction interval (1, 2)[cite: 51].
- Part C [1/1 pt]: Earned P6 for proving speeding up via matching positive signs of velocity and acceleration[cite: 51].
- Part D [3/3 pts]: Earned P7 for integral setup with initial position 7, P8 for correct antiderivative (via polynomial expansion), and P9 for final evaluated position 27[cite: 51].

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Calculus AB 2025 Question 6 (9 points total - No Calculator).
Topic: Implicit Differentiation, Tangent Line Linear Approximation, Vertical Tangent & Related Rates.
Given Curve G: y^3 - y^2 - y + (1/4)x^2 = 0. Particle Curve H: 2xy + ln y = 8 with dx/dt = 3 at (4, 1).
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A: (P1) Implicit differentiation of G: 3y^2(dy/dx) - 2y(dy/dx) - dy/dx + (1/2)x = 0; (P2) Verify: dy/dx = -x / [2(3y^2 - 2y - 1)].
- Part B: (P3) Slope at (2, -1): dy/dx = -2 / [2(3 + 2 - 1)] = -1/4; (P4) Tangent line approx at x = 1.6: y approx -1 - (1/4)(1.6 - 2) = -0.9.
- Part C: (P5) Set denominator to 0 for vertical tangent: 2(3y^2 - 2y - 1) = 0 -> (3y + 1)(y - 1) = 0; (P6) Solve for y > 0: y = 1.
- Part D: (P7) Differentiate 2xy + ln y = 8 with respect to t: 2y(dx/dt) + 2x(dy/dt) + (1/y)(dy/dt) = 0; (P8) Exact derivative equation; (P9) Substitute (4, 1, dx/dt=3) and solve: 2(1)(3) + 2(4)(dy/dt) + (1/1)(dy/dt) = 0 -> 6 + 9(dy/dt) = 0 -> dy/dt = -2/3.

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 6A) ===
Part A: y^3 - y^2 - y + (1/4)x^2 = 0 -> y^3 - y^2 - y = -(1/4)x^2. 3y^2(dy/dx) - 2y(dy/dx) - dy/dx = -(1/2)x -> dy/dx (3y^2 - 2y - 1) = -(1/2)x -> dy/dx = -x / [2(3y^2 - 2y - 1)]
Part B: dy/dx = -2 / [2(3(-1)^2 - 2(-1) - 1)] = -2 / [2(3 + 2 - 1)] = -2/8 = -1/4. y - (-1) = -(1/4)(x - 2) -> y + 1 = -(1/4)x + 1/2 -> y = -(1/4)x - 1/2. y approx -(1/4)(16/10) - 1/2 = -4/10 - 5/10 = -9/10 or -0.9
Part C: 2(3y^2 - 2y - 1) = 0 -> 3y^2 - 2y - 1 = 0 -> 3y^2 - 3y + y - 1 = 0 -> 3y(y - 1) + 1(y - 1) = 0 -> (3y + 1)(y - 1) = 0 -> 3y + 1 = 0 (y = -1/3), y - 1 = 0 (y = 1). The y-coordinate is 1 -> y = 1
Part D: (2x)(dy/dt) + (2dx/dt)(y) + (1/y)(dy/dt) = 0 -> 2(4)(dy/dt) + 2(3)(1) + (1/1)(dy/dt) = 0 -> 8(dy/dt) + 6 + dy/dt = 0 -> 9(dy/dt) = -6 -> dy/dt = -6/9 = -2/3
feedback:
Total Score: 9/9 points (Perfect Score: 1-1-1-1-1-1-1-1-1)[cite: 52].
- Part A [2/2 pts]: Earned P1 for implicit differentiation and P2 for algebraic verification of dy/dx[cite: 52].
- Part B [2/2 pts]: Earned P3 for tangent slope m = -1/4 and P4 for linear approximation y = -0.9 at x = 1.6[cite: 52].
- Part C [2/2 pts]: Earned P5 for setting denominator to 0 and P6 for identifying y = 1 for y > 0[cite: 52].
- Part D [3/3 pts]: Earned P7 and P8 for implicit differentiation with respect to t (product rule + chain rule), and P9 for evaluating dy/dt = -2/3[cite: 52].

Problem Context: Samples of 100 cars manufactured in Country A and 100 cars in Country B are evaluated for gas mileage (mpg). Country A has a lower median (18 mpg) and an outlier at 38 mpg. Country B has a median of 32 mpg, Q1 = 24 mpg, and max = 40 mpg. Q3 for Country A is 24 mpg, min is 14 mpg.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A (Compare Distributions): (1) Directly compare centers (Median A = 18 mpg < Median B = 32 mpg); (2) Directly compare spread (Range A = 24 mpg > Range B = 22 mpg OR IQR A = 8 mpg < IQR B = 12 mpg); (3) Indicate Country A has an outlier at 38 mpg while Country B has no outliers; (4) Provide context ('Country A/B' and 'gas mileage/mpg'). [Needs 3 of 4 for E]
- Part B (Mean vs. Median): (1) Indicate mean of Country A > 18 mpg; (2) Indicate 18 is the median; (3) Justify based on right-skewed shape or high outlier pulling the non-resistant mean above the resistant median. [Needs 3 of 3 for E]
- Part C (Combined Data Analysis): (i) Range = 40 - 14 = 26 mpg (Max = 40 from B, Min = 14 from A); (ii) Combined Median = 24 mpg (Justification: Q3 of A = 24 -> 75 cars <= 24; Q1 of B = 24 -> 25 cars <= 24; exactly 100 of 200 cars are <= 24 mpg). [Needs 4 of 4 for E]

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 1A) ===
A) The median gas mileage for Country A (18 mpg) is less than Country B (32 mpg). The IQR for Country A (8 mpg) is less than Country B (12 mpg). Country A has an outlier at 38 mpg, while Country B has no outliers.
B) It would be expected for the mean to be greater than 18 mpg because the distribution of gas mileage for Country A is skewed to the right and has an upper outlier at 38 mpg, which pulls the mean up.
C) (i) Range = 40 - 14 = 26 mpg. The max is 40 mpg from Country B and the min is 14 mpg from Country A.
(ii) A possible median of the combined dataset is 24 mpg. This is because 75% of Country A's dataset is <= 24 mpg (Q3, 75 cars) and 25% of Country B's dataset is <= 24 mpg (Q1, 25 cars). This adds to 100 cars out of 200 cars, which implies that 24 mpg is a possible median of the new dataset.
feedback:
Total Score: 4/4 points (Complete Response: Part A - E, Part B - E, Part C - E).
- Part A [E]: Correctly compared centers (median 18 vs 32), compared spread (IQR 8 vs 12), identified the 38 mpg outlier in Country A, and maintained complete context (mpg, countries).
- Part B [E]: Correctly stated mean > 18 mpg, identified 18 mpg as median, and provided valid justification based on right-skewness and the upper outlier.
- Part C [E]: Correctly calculated range (40 - 14 = 26 mpg) with minimum/maximum justifications, and accurately deduced combined median (24 mpg) with quartile count analysis (75 + 25 = 100 cars).

=== QUESTION & RUBRIC CONTEXT ===
Exam: AP Statistics 2025 Question 3 (4 points total).
Topic: Focus on Probability and Sampling Distributions (Independent Probabilities, Binomial Distribution & Probability Evidence Assessment).
Problem Context: A digital music station has 1,000 songs in its library, 100 of which are rock songs (p = 0.10). Any song can be replayed at any time (independence). A 1-hour block plays n = 20 songs. A manager suspects the shuffle algorithm is flawed when 4 rock songs play in one hour.
Rubric Expectations:
- Part A: (i) P(Rock) = 100/1,000 = 0.10; (ii) P(Both Rock) = (0.10)(0.10) = 0.01 with work shown. [Needs 4 of 4 for E]
- Part B: (i) Define X as number of rock songs played in 1 hour; (ii) State X ~ Binomial(n = 20, p = 0.10); (iii) E(X) = np = 20(0.10) = 2 songs with work. [Needs 3 of 4 for E]
- Part C: (i) P(X >= 4) = 1 - P(X <= 3) = 1 - 0.867 = 0.133 with binomial formula or labeled calculator syntax; (ii) State manager does not have strong evidence that shuffle is not random because p = 0.133 is large enough to reasonably occur by chance alone. [Needs 4 of 4 for E]

=== STUDENT RESPONSE (SAMPLE 3A) ===
A) i) P(rock) = 100 rock songs / 1000 total songs = 1/10 = 0.1. ii) P(rock twice) = P(rock) * P(rock) = (0.1)(0.1) = 0.01.
B) i) The random variable is the number of rock songs played out of 20 songs, and it is a binomial distribution.
ii) X = number of rock songs, n = total songs = 20, p = proportion of songs that are rock = 0.1. mu_X = np = 20(0.1) = 2. Expected value is 2 rock songs in an hour.
C) i) P(X >= 4) = 1 - P(X < 4) = 1 - (P(x=0) + P(x=1) + P(x=2) + P(x=3)) = 1 - [binompdf(20, 0.1, 0) + ... + binompdf(20, 0.1, 3)] = 1 - (0.867) = 0.133.
ii) This does not provide strong evidence that the selection process isn't random. There is a 13.3% chance of 4 or more rock songs playing in an hour, which is a high enough probability that it has a good chance of happening naturally given a random selection process.
feedback:
Total Score: 4/4 points (Complete Response: Part A - E, Part B - E, Part C - E).
- Part A [E]: Correctly calculated P(Rock) = 0.10 and P(Both Rock) = 0.01 with supporting multiplication.
- Part B [E]: Defined variable in context (rock songs out of 20), identified binomial model with n=20 and p=0.10, and calculated expected value E(X) = 2.
- Part C [E]: Correctly calculated cumulative binomial probability P(X >= 4) = 0.133 with expanded work, and correctly concluded that 13.3% is too likely to occur by chance to suggest non-randomness.
